title: Print an operand
starter:
type arg = Lit of int | Name of string

let show (a : arg) : string =
  match a with
  | Lit n -> ""
  | Name s -> "%" ^ s
hints: Only the `Lit` case is wrong. Inside it, `n` is the int that the `Lit` carries.
The function must return a string, and `n` is an int. Which function from O.1 turns an int into text?
explain: The reference has one case per kind: `Lit n -> string_of_int n` and `Name s -> "%" ^ s`. Each pattern both checks the kind and gives a name to the value inside it, so the right side can use that value.
